title: A linked list of tasks
description:
Keep tasks in a singly linked list.

```
added: write report, call Bob, buy milk
done: call Bob
list:
  [ ] write report
  [x] call Bob
  [ ] buy milk
removed done tasks: 1
list:
  [ ] write report
  [ ] buy milk
```
hints: A `Task **` lets the function change the caller's `head` when the list is empty (lesson 4.05).
`remove_done` walks with `Task **link = head;` and, for a done task, does `Task *gone = *link; *link = gone->next; free(gone);`, otherwise `link = &(*link)->next;`.
requirements: `typedef struct Task { char title[64]; int done; struct Task *next; } Task;`
`void push_back(Task **head, const char *title)`, `Task *find(Task *head, const char *title)`, `int remove_done(Task **head)` and `void free_all(Task *head)`.
Every `malloc` has a matching `free`; nothing leaks.
stretch: Keep the list sorted by title as tasks are added.
